stories.headline: Houthi Missile Attack on Yemeni Presidential Palace in Aden Kills Five
stories.summary:
Five people were killed and 16 injured when five ballistic missiles struck al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, the seat of Yemen's internationally recognised government, officials said. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt. Health Minister Qasim Buhaibeh said the casualties included guards and civilian employees at the site.

The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said the group struck what it called the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden. Prime Minister Shaya Zindani condemned the attack as cowardly and vowed that government forces would continue operations against the Houthis on the south-western Red Sea coast and other front lines. A Saudi-led coalition backs the government and is providing air support for a pro-government offensive.

The attack comes amid sharp escalation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia. Last Saturday a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, the deadliest attack in the kingdom in more than a decade. The coalition said it intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region on Thursday, though the Houthis denied attacking Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Rayed Krimly accused Iran of encouraging the escalation by arming and training the Houthis. Iran has denied supplying weapons and says it supports the group only politically, while its foreign minister said Tehran is ready to help facilitate talks between Riyadh and the Houthis. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July when the Houthis announced a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia.

stories.headline: Update: Ship Attacks Near Strait of Hormuz Reach Weekly Record as Oil Exports Slow
stories.summary:
Twelve vessels reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz between 5 and 11 October, the most in any week since the US-Israeli war with Iran began, according to BBC Verify analysis of UK Maritime Trade Operations data. The previous week saw 10 reported attacks, and four more have been reported so far this week. Six ships were struck on Sunday alone.

One of Sunday's attacks hit the Nicaragua-flagged tanker Petro Dolphin with a drone near Oman's Sohar Anchorage, more than 250km from the strait. Eleven Indian seafarers were rescued but two remain missing, according to a seafarers' union. On Tuesday the container ship GFS Pride sank after being hit by an unknown projectile, and its 21 crew were evacuated. Iran's Revolutionary Guard published footage of the sinking and said the ship carried contraband on an unauthorised route.

Experts say Tehran is trying to assert greater control over the waterway as the US military escorts more tankers through the southern part of the strait. US Central Command said commercial traffic continues to flow with coordinated protection from US forces and regional partners.

Oil flows have nonetheless slowed. About 12.6 million barrels per day passed through the strait on 13 October, according to Kpler, down from 15 million at the end of September and well below the pre-war baseline of roughly 17 million. The slowdown adds pressure to energy prices already driving US inflation.

stories.headline: Update: Ukraine Abandons Energy Truce and Strikes Russian Refinery as Trump Calls Move 'a Disgrace'
stories.summary:
Ukraine attacked a Russian oil refinery after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv was abandoning an energy-target ceasefire that President Trump had demanded last Sunday. Kyiv said Moscow never honored the truce and continued its own attacks.

Trump called the renewed Ukrainian strikes on refineries a disgrace and said Zelenskyy is more difficult to deal with than Vladimir Putin. Coverage describes the relationship between the two leaders as nearing a new low after days of public exchanges. Ukraine also said satellite internet via Starshield, the military version of Starlink, had resumed at previous speeds for the moment after earlier speed limits that Kyiv said hampered its defense against Russian drones.

The collapse of the truce removes a short-lived pause in attacks on energy infrastructure, which has been a central feature of the war. Russian strikes had left about 600,000 people without power in Ukraine despite the announced ceasefire. Supporters of the administration's approach say Trump is pressing both sides toward a settlement, while Kyiv and its European backers say Moscow was never constrained and that Ukraine has the right to hit refineries that fuel Russia's war effort.

stories.headline: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Confirms She Did Not Pass the Bar Exam
stories.summary:
White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said late Thursday that she did not pass the bar exam, after questions arose about her legal background before joining the Trump administration. Zacharia had previously claimed to be a lawyer, and President Trump has described her as an attorney. The scrutiny came during her first week in the job.

BBC reporting noted she does not appear to be registered with the legal bar in any state where she has lived. A spokesperson for the State Bar of California told NBC News the bar cannot confirm whether it has received a complaint or is conducting an investigation, citing confidentiality rules. A different group had asked the bar to investigate her.

The White House referred reporters to a post by communications director Steven Cheung, who criticized the group that requested the investigation. Administration allies have framed the questions as a partisan attack on a new spokesperson, while critics say a public official misrepresenting credentials raises credibility concerns. Zacharia's tenure began amid the announced resignation request involving Kimberly Guilfoyle, which she disclosed at a briefing.
